cards.prompt: What is the format of the Salesforce Platform Administrator exam?
answer: 60 scored multiple-choice/multiple-select questions + 5 unscored, 105 minutes, 68% to pass
cards.why: From the instructor's notes. The real exam is proctored and closed book; practice exams need 95%+.

cards.prompt: Configuration and Setup (15%, ~9 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Company settings (fiscal year, business hours, currency, defaults); UI config (app menu, list views, global actions, Lightning App Builder); user setup (unique username, locales, licenses, never delete, inactive, feature licenses, login methods); security controls (identity verification, Setup Audit Trail, login hours, session settings, agent access); sharing model (teams, hierarchy, public groups, OWD, roles, report/dashboard folders); profiles vs. permission sets (permission set groups, muting)
cards.why: Exam 2 score here: 100%. Core rule: profiles/permission sets = what you can DO; sharing = which RECORDS you can SEE.

cards.prompt: Data and Analytics Management (17%, ~10-11 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Importing, updating, transferring, mass deleting, exporting, backing up (archival, Data Loader, Import Wizard); validation tools (duplicate and matching rules, validation rules); reports (report types, with/without, formulas, buckets, joined reports, charts, grouping); sharing impact on reports (folders); dashboards (components, sources, subscribing, dynamic dashboards, view as, scheduled refresh, filters)

cards.prompt: Productivity and Collaboration (10%, ~6 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Activity management (tasks, events); Chatter (groups, group access, internal/external users); Salesforce mobile app (Lightning pages, app menu, visibility, branding, launchpad); AppExchange (managed vs. unmanaged packages, who can publish, AgentExchange, flows)
cards.why: Weakest area on Exam 2 (17%). Study first.

cards.prompt: Service and Support Applications (10%, ~6 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Case management (cases, case assignment rules, queues); automating case management (support process, auto-response rules, escalation, Einstein for Service)

cards.prompt: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder (15%, ~9 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Standard object architecture and relationships (parent/child, master-detail, lookup, junction, record types, Schema Builder); creating, deleting, customizing fields and layouts (roll-ups, cross-object formulas, picklist dependencies, relationship fields); page layouts, Lightning page visibility, record types, business processes, quick and global actions

cards.prompt: Sales and Marketing Applications (10%, ~6 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Sales process (leads, opportunities, path); opportunity tools (dashboards, lead scoring, Einstein for Sales, opportunity scoring, forecasting, territory management); lead automation and campaigns (lead convert, lead assignment rules, campaigns, campaign members)

cards.prompt: Automation (15%, ~9 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Choosing the right tool (escalation rules, case/lead assignment rules, default automation user, AI); Flow (screen, record-triggered, autolaunched, order of execution); approval processes (approver criteria, approvals, rejections)

cards.prompt: Agentforce (8%, ~5 Qs): what does it cover?
answer: Capabilities and use cases (when AI is appropriate, security, troubleshooting agent permissions); maintaining and installing prompts and instructions in Agent Builder (light testing, Conversation Preview)
cards.why: Exam 2 score: 60%. Rule: language and judgment → AI; strict rules and compliance → Flow.
